inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” organizers are claiming 8 million people turned out across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states—but that figure comes from the organizers, not an official count. The authorities’ silence leaves plenty of room for competing narratives, and the headline is already doing its job: turning a disputed estimate into proof of a nationwide uprising. Their claim that turnout was up “about one million” and 600 events from October makes the scale sound undeniable, but it’s still a claim from the people promoting the protests. The real story may be less about a verified head count than about who gets to define public opinion.
